questions.stem: Insurance is best described as a device by which
options: one person makes a profit from another person's loss
the government pays for every loss
the losses of a few are shared by many who pay into a common fund
losses are prevented from ever happening
questions.explanation: Insurance pools premiums from many to pay the losses of the unfortunate few.

questions.stem: The two main parties to an insurance contract are the
questions.explanation: The insurer accepts the risk; the insured pays the premium.

questions.stem: A risk that can result only in loss or no loss, such as a house catching fire, is a
questions.explanation: Pure risks offer no chance of gain, so they are insurable.

questions.stem: Which of the following risks is NOT normally insurable?
options: Damage to a car in an accident
Loss from a fall in the price of shares a trader bought
Theft of goods from a shop
Injury to a worker at work
questions.explanation: Losses from speculation in prices are speculative risks and are not insurable.

questions.stem: Poor housekeeping, such as storing petrol beside a kitchen stove, is an example of a
questions.explanation: A physical hazard is a tangible condition that increases the chance of loss.

questions.stem: A policyholder who becomes careless about locking his shop because he knows he is insured shows
questions.explanation: Moral hazard arises from the attitude or behaviour of the insured.

questions.stem: In the statement "Lightning struck the factory and set it on fire", lightning and fire are best described as
questions.explanation: A peril is the actual cause of a loss.

questions.stem: The insurance market at Lloyd's of London began in
questions.explanation: Lloyd's grew from Edward Lloyd's coffee house where merchants and underwriters met.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a SECONDARY function of insurance?
options: Transferring risk from the insured to the insurer
Creating a common pool of premiums
Providing funds for investment in the economy
questions.explanation: Investment of funds is a secondary (indirect) benefit; risk transfer and pooling are primary functions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a benefit of insurance to a business?
options: It guarantees that the business will make a profit
It gives peace of mind and enables the business to continue after a loss
It removes the need for safety measures
It stops competitors from entering the market
questions.explanation: Insurance restores the business financially after an insured loss.

questions.stem: Insurable interest means that the insured
options: would suffer financial loss if the insured property is damaged
has paid a premium for many years
questions.explanation: The insured must stand to lose financially from the loss.

questions.stem: In life assurance, insurable interest must exist
options: at the start of the policy
only at the time of death
at the start and every month
only when the claim is paid
questions.explanation: For life assurance, insurable interest is needed only at inception.

questions.stem: In marine insurance, insurable interest must exist
options: at the time of the loss
only when the proposal form is signed
only when the ship is built
questions.explanation: Marine cargo often changes hands during a voyage, so interest is required at the time of loss.

questions.stem: The principle that requires both parties to disclose all material facts is
questions.explanation: Uberrimae fidei requires full and true disclosure.

questions.stem: A material fact is one that
options: is written in large print on the policy
would influence the insurer in accepting the risk or fixing the premium
is known only to the broker
relates to the colour of the property
questions.explanation: Material facts affect the underwriter's decision.

questions.stem: If a proposer deliberately hides a material fact, the insurer may
questions.explanation: Fraudulent concealment makes the contract voidable at the insurer's option.

questions.stem: Proximate cause refers to the
options: last event that happened just before the loss
cause nearest in distance to the loss
active and efficient cause that sets in motion a chain of events leading to the loss
questions.explanation: It is the dominant, effective cause, not necessarily the latest in time.

questions.stem: A storm (an insured peril) blew down an electric pole, causing a fire that destroyed a shop. Under the principle of proximate cause, the loss is caused by the
questions.explanation: The storm started the unbroken chain of events, so it is the proximate cause.

questions.stem: The principle of indemnity aims to
options: allow the insured to make a profit from the loss
put the insured back in the same financial position as before the loss
punish the person who caused the loss
questions.explanation: Indemnity restores the insured without profit.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a method by which an insurer may provide indemnity?
options: Paying the insured double the value of the loss
questions.explanation: Indemnity may be given by cash, repair, replacement or reinstatement, never by over-compensation.

questions.stem: A building worth ₦2,000,000 is insured for ₦1,500,000 under a policy subject to average. A fire causes damage of ₦400,000. The insurer will pay
questions.explanation: Claim = 1,500,000/2,000,000 x 400,000 = ₦300,000 because of under-insurance.

questions.stem: Subrogation gives the insurer the right to
options: take over the insured's rights against a third party after paying the claim
cancel the policy at any time
ask other insurers to share the loss
increase the premium after a claim
questions.explanation: After indemnifying, the insurer stands in the insured's place.

questions.stem: Subrogation arises only
options: before the proposal form is signed
when the insured has no policy
after the insurer has indemnified the insured
questions.explanation: The insurer must first pay the claim before exercising subrogation rights.

questions.stem: Subrogation does NOT normally apply to life assurance because
options: there is no premium in life assurance
life assurance is not a contract of indemnity
questions.explanation: A human life cannot be valued exactly, so life policies pay a fixed sum, not an indemnity.

questions.stem: Contribution applies where
options: the insured has no insurable interest
the same interest in the same property is insured with two or more insurers against the same peril
questions.explanation: The insurers share the loss ratably.

questions.stem: A shop is insured against fire with Insurer A for ₦600,000 and Insurer B for ₦400,000. A fire causes a loss of ₦250,000. Under contribution, Insurer A pays
The purpose of the principle of contribution is to
options: make each insurer pay the full loss
reduce premiums for all insured persons
transfer rights to a third party
prevent the insured from recovering more than the actual loss from several insurers
questions.explanation: Contribution supports indemnity by sharing the loss.

questions.stem: The document completed by a person who wants insurance, giving details of the risk, is the
questions.explanation: The proposal form is the basis of the contract.

questions.stem: The person who completes and signs a proposal form is the
questions.explanation: The proposer becomes the insured once the proposal is accepted.

questions.stem: The declaration at the end of a proposal form is important because it
options: states the amount of claim payable
transfers the risk to a reinsurer
makes the answers given the basis of the contract
questions.explanation: By signing, the proposer confirms the truth of the answers, linking them to utmost good faith.

questions.stem: A cover note is
options: a temporary document showing that insurance cover is in force until the policy is issued
a receipt for a claim payment
questions.explanation: It gives interim cover.

questions.stem: Cover notes are NOT normally used in
questions.explanation: Life assurance cover usually starts when the proposal is accepted and the first premium paid.

questions.stem: In motor insurance, the certificate of insurance serves mainly as
options: a receipt for the vehicle purchase
legal evidence that the vehicle has the compulsory insurance cover
questions.explanation: Police and road authorities check the certificate as proof of cover.

questions.stem: Under a marine open cover for many shipments, each consignment is usually evidenced by a
questions.explanation: Certificates are issued for individual shipments declared under the open cover.

questions.stem: The formal document that contains the terms and conditions of an insurance contract is the
questions.explanation: The policy is the evidence of the contract.

questions.stem: The part of a policy that contains details such as the name of the insured, sum insured and period of insurance is the
questions.explanation: The schedule holds the specific details of each insured.

questions.stem: The part of a policy that states what the insurer agrees to cover is the
questions.explanation: The operative clause sets out the cover provided.

questions.stem: Re-insurance means
options: an insurer insuring part of its own risk with another insurer
questions.explanation: Reinsurance is insurance for insurers.

questions.stem: A reinsurance arrangement under which each risk is offered to and accepted by the reinsurer individually is
questions.explanation: In facultative reinsurance, each risk is negotiated separately.

questions.stem: A main advantage of treaty reinsurance over facultative reinsurance is that
options: the reinsurer may reject each risk
it is only used for life assurance
risks within the treaty are covered automatically without separate negotiation
questions.explanation: Treaties provide automatic cover for agreed classes of business.

questions.stem: A letter sent by an insurer reminding the insured that the policy is due for renewal is a
questions.explanation: The renewal notice invites renewal.

questions.stem: A discount on the premium given to a motor policyholder who made no claim in the previous year is
questions.explanation: NCD rewards claim-free years.

questions.stem: Under a Long Term Agreement (LTA), the insured agrees to
options: renew the policy with the same insurer for a number of years in return for a discount
questions.explanation: LTAs give a discount for loyalty over an agreed number of years.

questions.stem: The first duty of the insured after a loss is to
options: repair the property before informing anyone
ask for a refund of premiums
questions.explanation: Prompt notice allows the insurer to investigate.

questions.stem: A document signed by the insured to acknowledge receipt of the claim payment in full settlement is a
questions.explanation: The discharge voucher ends the insurer's liability for that claim.

questions.stem: A loss adjuster differs from a loss assessor in that the loss adjuster
options: is appointed by the insurer, while the assessor acts for the insured
is appointed by the insured, while the assessor acts for the insurer
questions.explanation: Adjusters negotiate claims on behalf of insurers; assessors represent claimants.

questions.stem: The price paid by the insured for insurance cover is the
questions.explanation: Premium is the consideration for the insurer's promise.

questions.stem: Adding an extra charge to the normal premium because the risk is above average is called
questions.explanation: Loading reflects higher hazards.

questions.stem: Part of the premium is refunded to the insured when a policy is cancelled before it expires. This is
questions.explanation: Return premium may be full or partial depending on the circumstances.

questions.stem: The minimum motor insurance required by law in Nigeria covers
options: damage to the insured's own car
questions.explanation: Third party motor insurance is compulsory.

questions.stem: A motor policy that covers third party liability as well as loss or damage to the insured's own vehicle is
questions.explanation: Comprehensive is the widest motor cover.

questions.stem: The ECOWAS Brown Card is
options: a driving licence for West Africa
a motor insurance scheme that covers third party liability when a vehicle travels to other ECOWAS countries
questions.explanation: It guarantees third party cover for motorists across member states.

questions.stem: Which of the following perils is covered by a standard fire policy?
questions.explanation: Fire, lightning and limited explosion are standard; earthquake, flood and riot are special perils added by extension.

questions.stem: A factory owner in an area prone to flooding wants flood damage covered under his fire policy. He should
options: take out a personal accident policy
rely on the standard fire policy
add flood as a special peril by extension and pay extra premium
questions.explanation: Special perils are added by endorsement for an extra premium.

questions.stem: Burglary insurance differs from ordinary theft insurance because burglary requires
options: forcible and violent entry into or exit from the premises
questions.explanation: Burglary cover usually requires forcible entry or exit.

questions.stem: Which of the following is covered by household burglary insurance?
options: Damage to a car in a crash
questions.explanation: Household contents stolen through forcible entry are covered.

questions.stem: A money insurance policy usually covers
options: cash and cheques in transit and in a locked safe
questions.explanation: Money insurance protects cash and negotiable instruments.

questions.stem: Fidelity guarantee insurance protects an employer against loss caused by
questions.explanation: It covers fraud and embezzlement by staff.

questions.stem: A fidelity guarantee policy covering ALL employees without naming them is a
questions.explanation: Blanket policies cover all staff; position policies cover posts; named policies cover named persons.

questions.stem: Which policy covers loss from the sudden breakdown or explosion of a boiler?
questions.explanation: Engineering insurance covers boilers, machinery and computers.

questions.stem: Marine insurance that covers the ship itself is
questions.explanation: Hull insurance covers the vessel.

questions.stem: Which of these is a marine peril?
options: Sinking of the vessel in a storm
questions.explanation: Perils of the sea include sinking, stranding and heavy weather.

questions.stem: The Montreal Convention is an international agreement that deals mainly with
questions.explanation: It updated the Warsaw system on airline liability for passengers, baggage and cargo.

questions.stem: Employer's liability insurance covers an employer's legal liability for
options: injury to members of the public
injury or disease suffered by employees in the course of their work
questions.explanation: It covers employees' work-related injuries.

questions.stem: A supermarket customer slips on a wet floor and sues the owner. The policy that covers this is
questions.explanation: Public liability covers legal liability to third parties.

questions.stem: Professional indemnity insurance is most suitable for
questions.explanation: It covers liability for professional negligence.

questions.stem: Business interruption insurance is also called
questions.explanation: It covers loss of profit following damage.

questions.stem: Which of these is covered by personal accident insurance?
options: Permanent disability caused by an accident
questions.explanation: PA covers death, injury and disability from accidents.

questions.stem: An insurance broker is an intermediary who
options: is an employee of the regulator
acts on behalf of the insured to arrange the best cover
questions.explanation: Brokers are professional agents of the insured.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an insurance intermediary?
questions.explanation: Agents and brokers are intermediaries between insurers and buyers.

questions.stem: Companies that insure other insurance companies are called
questions.explanation: Reinsurers accept part of the risks of direct insurers.

questions.stem: Which of these is a supporting service in the insurance market?
questions.explanation: Loss adjusters and assessors support the market in claims settlement.

questions.stem: The government body that regulates and supervises insurance business in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The National Insurance Commission is the regulator.

questions.stem: The professional body responsible for training and examining insurance professionals in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: CIIN educates and certifies insurance professionals.

questions.stem: The NCRIB is the body for
questions.explanation: NCRIB means Nigerian Council of Registered Insurance Brokers.

questions.stem: Membership of the Nigerian Insurers Association (NIA) is made up of
questions.explanation: The NIA is the trade association of insurance and reinsurance companies.

questions.stem: A payment made by an insurer as a goodwill gesture, although it is not legally liable, is an
questions.explanation: Ex-gratia payments are made out of goodwill.

questions.stem: A written alteration to the terms of an existing policy is called an
questions.explanation: Endorsements change policy terms during its term.

questions.stem: The amount payable to a policyholder who ends a life assurance policy before maturity is the
questions.explanation: Surrender value is the cash value of the policy on early termination.

questions.stem: The period allowed after the renewal date during which premium can be paid without losing cover is the
questions.explanation: Days of grace allow late payment while keeping cover in force.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of risk. [2 marks]
(b) Distinguish between: (i) pure risk and speculative risk; (ii) fundamental risk and particular risk. [6 marks]
(c) State four characteristics of an insurable risk. [4 marks]
(d) Distinguish between peril and hazard. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) the uncertainty or possibility of a loss occurring
3 marks: (b)(i) pure risk results in loss or no loss (e.g. fire); speculative risk may result in loss, no loss or gain (e.g. gambling, trading)
3 marks: (b)(ii) fundamental risk affects society or large groups and arises from impersonal causes (e.g. war, inflation); particular risk affects individuals and arises from personal causes (e.g. burglary)
4 marks: (c) any four: financial value measurable; large number of similar risks; loss must be accidental/fortuitous; insurable interest; not against public policy; premium affordable (1 mark each)
3 marks: (d) peril is the actual cause of loss (e.g. fire); hazard is a condition that increases the chance or severity of loss (e.g. storing petrol at home)
questions.explanation: Risk is the possibility of loss. Pure risk gives loss or no loss; speculative may give gain. Fundamental risk affects society; particular risk affects individuals. Insurable risks are measurable, accidental, numerous, lawful and backed by insurable interest. A peril causes loss; a hazard increases its chance.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the principle of utmost good faith. [3 marks]
(b) State four material facts that a proposer for motor insurance should disclose. [4 marks]
(c) State two duties of disclosure owed by the insurer. [4 marks]
(d) Explain two forms of breach of utmost good faith and their effect on the contract. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) both parties must voluntarily disclose all material facts accurately and completely, whether asked or not
4 marks: (b) any four: age and experience of the driver; previous accidents/claims; use of the vehicle; value of the vehicle; convictions for driving offences; modifications (1 mark each)
4 marks: (c) any two, 2 marks each: disclose terms and conditions of the policy; explain exclusions; not to misrepresent the cover; inform of reductions in premium available
2 marks: (d) non-disclosure/concealment: failing to reveal a material fact; contract voidable at the option of the aggrieved party
2 marks: (d) misrepresentation: a false statement of a material fact, innocent or fraudulent; fraudulent breach makes the contract voidable and premiums may be forfeited
questions.explanation: Utmost good faith requires full disclosure of material facts by both parties. A motor proposer should disclose driver details, previous claims, use and value of the vehicle and convictions. The insurer must disclose terms and exclusions. Non-disclosure and misrepresentation make the contract voidable.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the principle of contribution. [3 marks]
(b) State three conditions necessary for contribution to apply. [6 marks]
(c) Chika insured her shop against fire with Unity Insurance for ₦900,000 and with Bright Insurance for ₦600,000. A fire caused damage of ₦300,000. Calculate the amount each insurer will pay under contribution. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) where the insured has more than one policy covering the same loss, each insurer pays a ratable share so that the insured is not paid more than the loss
6 marks: (b) any three, 2 marks each: two or more policies must exist; they must cover the same interest; the same subject matter; the same peril; all policies must be in force at the time of loss
2 marks: (c) total sum insured ₦1,500,000
2 marks: (c) Unity: 900,000/1,500,000 x 300,000 = ₦180,000
2 marks: (c) Bright: 600,000/1,500,000 x 300,000 = ₦120,000
questions.explanation: Contribution makes insurers covering the same loss share it ratably. Conditions: two or more policies, same interest, subject matter and peril, all in force. Unity pays 900/1500 x 300,000 = ₦180,000; Bright pays ₦120,000.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of a proposal form. [2 marks]
(b) State four functions of a proposal form. [4 marks]
(c) Explain the meaning of a cover note and state three of its contents. [5 marks]
(d) State two classes of insurance where cover notes are commonly issued. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) a form completed by a prospective insured giving details of the risk, which forms the basis of the contract
4 marks: (b) any four: provides information to assess the risk; basis of the contract; helps fix premium; evidence of disclosure; identifies the proposer and subject matter (1 mark each)
2 marks: (c) a temporary document giving evidence of cover until the policy is issued
3 marks: (c) any three: name of insured; period of cover; subject matter; type of cover; signature of insurer; cover note number (1 mark each)
4 marks: (d) any two: motor; fire; burglary; marine; accident (2 marks each)
questions.explanation: A proposal form gives the insurer information to assess the risk and is the basis of the contract. A cover note is temporary evidence of insurance showing insured, period, subject matter and cover. Cover notes are common in motor and fire insurance.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of an insurance claim. [2 marks]
(b) Describe the procedure for settling a claim. [8 marks]
(c) State the functions of a loss adjuster. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) a formal demand by the insured for payment under a policy after an insured loss
2 marks: (b) notification: insured informs the insurer promptly
2 marks: (b) documentation: insured completes the claim form and provides supporting documents
2 marks: (b) investigation: insurer or loss adjuster verifies the cause and amount of loss
2 marks: (b) discharge voucher is signed and payment is made
5 marks: (c) any five: investigates the cause of loss; checks that the loss is covered; assesses the amount of loss; negotiates settlement; advises the insurer; prevents fraud; recommends salvage (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: A claim is a request for payment after an insured loss. Procedure: notification, claim form and documents, investigation by insurer or adjuster, then discharge voucher and payment. Loss adjusters investigate, verify cover, assess and negotiate on behalf of insurers.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the meaning of re-insurance. [3 marks]
(b) Distinguish between facultative and treaty re-insurance. [6 marks]
(c) State three functions of re-insurance. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) the process whereby an insurer transfers part of the risk it has accepted to another insurer (reinsurer)
3 marks: (b) facultative: each risk is offered individually and the reinsurer is free to accept or reject it
3 marks: (b) treaty: an agreement under which risks of a defined class are automatically ceded and accepted
6 marks: (c) any three, 2 marks each: spreads risk; increases capacity to accept large risks; stabilises results; protects against catastrophe losses; provides technical advice
questions.explanation: Reinsurance is insurance for insurers. Facultative reinsurance is negotiated risk by risk; treaty reinsurance is automatic for agreed classes. It spreads risk, increases capacity, stabilises results and protects against catastrophes.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the following scopes of motor insurance cover: (i) Act only; (ii) third party, fire and theft; (iii) comprehensive. [9 marks]
(b) Explain the meaning and use of the ECOWAS Brown Card. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a)(i) Act only: the minimum cover required by law, covering liability for death or bodily injury to third parties
3 marks: (a)(ii) third party, fire and theft: third party liability plus loss or damage to the insured's vehicle by fire or theft
3 marks: (a)(iii) comprehensive: third party liability plus accidental damage, fire and theft of the insured's own vehicle
3 marks: (b) a regional motor insurance scheme of ECOWAS member states
3 marks: (b) it gives motorists travelling to other member countries third party cover and prompt settlement of claims there
questions.explanation: Act only covers legal minimum third party injury liability; TPFT adds fire and theft of own vehicle; comprehensive adds accidental damage to own vehicle. The ECOWAS Brown Card provides third party motor cover and claims handling for motorists across member states.

questions.stem:
Read the case study and answer the questions.
Alhaji Musa owns a two-storey warehouse in Kano stocked with rice and sugar worth ₦40,000,000. The building is worth ₦30,000,000. He took out a standard fire policy on the building for ₦30,000,000 and on the stock for ₦24,000,000, both subject to average. During the harmattan, a fire started from an electrical fault and destroyed stock worth ₦10,000,000. The building was slightly damaged, costing ₦2,000,000 to repair. Alhaji Musa kept fuel for his generator inside the warehouse.
(a) Identify the peril and the hazard in the case. [4 marks]
(b) Calculate the amount payable for: (i) the building; (ii) the stock. [8 marks]
(c) Explain the principle that reduced the claim in (b)(ii). [4 marks]
(d) State two special perils that could be added to the fire policy. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: (a) peril: fire (from the electrical fault)
2 marks: (a) hazard: storing generator fuel inside the warehouse (physical hazard)
3 marks: (b)(i) building fully insured (₦30m sum insured equals value), so payment = ₦2,000,000
1 mark: (b)(ii) stock underinsured: sum insured ₦24m, value ₦40m
4 marks: (b)(ii) 24,000,000/40,000,000 x 10,000,000 = ₦6,000,000
4 marks: (c) average (under-insurance): where the sum insured is less than the value at risk, the insured bears a ratable share of the loss, in line with the principle of indemnity
4 marks: (d) any two: earthquake; flood; riot and strike; storm; malicious damage; bush fire (2 marks each)
questions.explanation: The peril is fire; the hazard is fuel stored in the warehouse. The building is fully insured, so ₦2,000,000 is paid. Stock is under-insured: 24/40 x 10,000,000 = ₦6,000,000. The average condition reduced the stock claim. Special perils include flood, earthquake and riot.

questions.stem:
(a) State the full meaning of NAICOM and CIIN. [2 marks]
(b) State four functions of the National Insurance Commission. [8 marks]
(c) State five functions of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: (a) NAICOM: National Insurance Commission
1 mark: (a) CIIN: Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria
8 marks: (b) any four, 2 marks each: licensing/registration of insurers and intermediaries; supervision and regulation of insurance business; protecting policyholders; approving rates and policy terms; ensuring solvency of insurers; setting standards; advising government on insurance
5 marks: (c) any five: training and educating insurance professionals; conducting professional examinations; awarding certificates/fellowships; promoting professional ethics; research and publications; organising seminars (1 mark each)
questions.explanation: NAICOM is the National Insurance Commission; CIIN is the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria. NAICOM licenses, supervises and regulates insurers and protects policyholders. CIIN trains, examines and certifies insurance professionals and promotes ethics.

questions.stem: Explain the following insurance terms: (a) under-insurance; (b) days of grace; (c) ex-gratia payment; (d) endorsement; (e) subject matter of insurance. [15 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: (a) under-insurance: where the sum insured is less than the actual value of the property; the insured bears part of any loss
3 marks: (b) days of grace: an extra period after the renewal date allowed for payment of premium during which cover may continue
3 marks: (c) ex-gratia payment: a payment made by an insurer out of goodwill when it has no legal liability to pay
3 marks: (d) endorsement: a written alteration added to a policy to change its terms
3 marks: (e) subject matter: the property, life or liability that is insured
questions.explanation: Under-insurance means the sum insured is below value, so average applies. Days of grace allow late premium payment. Ex-gratia is a goodwill payment without liability. An endorsement alters a policy. The subject matter is the item, life or liability insured.
